subject: GPT-6.1 Sol, released 2026-09-29
central_claim: GPT-6.1 Sol is a publishable AI engineering topic because OpenAI's announcement, API changelog, model page, GPT-6 guide and system-card addendum support a bounded E2/R1 claim: OpenAI has repositioned Sol as a lower-cost middle model for long coding, computer-use and professional agent workflows, with concrete engineering consequences around Responses API tool calling, cache economics, reasoning effort, context limits, data residency and safety safeguards. The article does not claim independent benchmark superiority, reproducible cost savings or independently verified safeguard effectiveness.

selection.reason: GPT-6.1 Sol was released on 2026-09-29 and directly affects teams choosing model routing for coding agents, computer use, long-context document work and cost-sensitive automations. Multiple official primary sources identify the model ID, API support, pricing, limits, migration constraints and safety assessment. Korean-reader relevance is scored 1 because availability and data-processing choices depend on each organization's OpenAI account, region and compliance needs, but Korean software teams commonly use OpenAI API and Codex-like agent workflows.

claims.claim: GPT-6.1 Sol changes model-routing decisions for long coding and computer-use agents by offering an officially documented lower-cost middle tier between Astra and Luna, while requiring engineering checks around Responses API tool calling, reasoning effort, caching, context limits and safeguards.

claim_source_ledger.method: Opened the official changelog and checked the September 29 entry for model ID, supported APIs, release description, pricing note and multi-agent note.

conflict_of_interest: OpenAI develops and sells GPT-6.1 Sol.

claim_source_ledger.claim: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol system-card addendum treats GPT-6.1 Sol as Critical capability in cybersecurity and High capability in biological and chemical domains, and says it applies the same safeguards stack as GPT-6 Astra.
claim_source_ledger.version: Addendum to GPT-6 Astra System Card: GPT-6.1 Sol, published 2026-09-29
claim_source_ledger.method: Opened the public Deployment Safety Hub page and checked Introduction and Preparedness sections. Also reviewed visible cybersecurity and biological evaluation passages.
limitations: The addendum is authored by OpenAI and includes internal evaluations.
Raw logs, full evaluation harnesses and production safeguard-effectiveness data were not reproduced.

benchmark_and_reproducibility.benchmark_notes: The article quotes only a small number of OpenAI-reported safety/cyber evaluation figures from the system-card addendum to explain deployment constraints. It does not build a cross-vendor leaderboard or declare independent model superiority. Performance and cost claims are attributed to OpenAI's own documents.
benchmark_and_reproducibility.reproducibility_notes: The announcement, API changelog, model page, GPT-6 guide, model-selection page and system-card addendum are public. Reproducing the core model performance, cost-per-task claims or safeguard results would require access to proprietary model deployments, internal evaluation tasks, raw logs and hidden operational settings.
